# Duration weights (seconds) for the self-host e2e shard partition —
# consumed by scripts/selfhost-shard-tests (greedy LPT). Only tests that
# are meaningfully slower than the ~0.1-1s norm need an entry; everything
# else defaults to weight 1. Staleness is benign: a wrong/missing/extra
# entry only skews shard BALANCE (the partition always covers the real
# -test.list output), so update opportunistically when a shard's log
# shows a test dominating its wall-clock, not religiously.
#
# Baseline heavy entries measured on the x86_64 ubuntu-latest lane with
# all drivers warm (2026-07-11, run 29157258229); the IR / wasm mid-tier
# and the wasmtime-gated entries added from run 29165757576 (the first
# with wasmtime restored to the shards).
#
# NOTE on the TestSelfHostExtern* family: those ~39 tests each build a
# stdin driver that is byte-identical to the stock wasm_runio_run.fern,
# which the `wasm*` warm jobs prime — so post-conversion each restores
# the driver (~1s) and its remaining cost is just its own wasmtime +
# wasm-tools compose run (~5-10s). They no longer need per-test weights;
# left at the default 1 unless a shard log shows them dominating again.

# Whole-compiler self-builds / fixpoints — the genuine multi-minute tail.
TestSelfHostModloadPerModuleWholeCompilerX86_64 210
# Two whole-compiler emit-all passes at batch=4 (gen0 40 s + gen1 79 s),
# measured on the x86_64 lane 2026-07-29 with the modload driver warm. Well
# above the ~1 s norm, so LPT gives it its own bucket rather than stacking it
# behind another fixpoint; still under the entry above, so it does not set the
# max-shard wall.
TestSelfHostPerModuleEmitAllFixpointBatch4X86_64 130
# Two warm drivers (asm_ir_run + wasm_ir_run), 14 subtests that are ~0.01s each —
# the cost is almost entirely the driver restore.
TestSelfHostFnArrayFieldGateX86_64 12
TestSelfHostFnArrayFieldGateWasm 12
TestSelfHostTupleFnZeroArgIRX86_64 12
TestSelfHostTupleFnZeroArgIRWasm 12
TestSelfHostAsmX86_64 90
TestSelfHostModloadPerModuleWholeCompilerArm64 80
TestSelfHostLoadFixpointX86_64 75
TestSelfHostFieldReclaimIRX86_64 55
TestSelfHostAsmIRPath 28
TestSelfHostStage2FixedPoint 27
TestSelfHostModloadFixpointX86_64 18
TestSelfHostStdTestE2E 18

# Tuple element from a wide-returning call (#5902): 7 subtests through two
# drivers (asm_run + asm_pathprobe_run). MEASURED 2.6 s with both restored from
# the warm cache, per the FERN_SELFHOST_BUILD_CACHE method documented on the
# interp-driver entry below — a cold `go test` reports 249 s, 94x higher,
# because it re-emits both drivers.
TestSelfHostTupleWideCallElem 3
# The interp driver (#5912): self-host-compiles lexer + parser + interp + util
# into a working interpreter, then feeds it 104 tiny programs. MEASURED 6.58 s
# with the modload driver restored from the warm cache, which is what the shard
# step configures via FERN_SELFHOST_BUILD_CACHE.
#
# Recorded because the naive measurement is off by ~23x and I nearly wrote it
# here: `go test` with no FERN_SELFHOST_BUILD_CACHE has NO disk cache at all
# (diskCacheReadDirs returns nil), so it re-emits the ~245 MB driver every
# invocation and reports ~140-155 s. Almost all of that is the driver build the
# warm artifact eliminates. To reproduce the real number, point the var at a dir
# already holding `<hash>.driverbin` — note the suffix, `drv-<hash>` is the
# separate link cache and will silently MISS.
#
# This test had no entry while it was segfaulting on every integer literal
# (#5901, fixed by #5908), so its 18-minute shard-11 blowout was the hang, not a
# scheduling error. 6.58 s is the honest cost; the entry is ordinary balance.
TestSelfHostInterpDriverX86_64 7
